messages:
maya: thinking out loud — we should discuss a JIT snapshot export flow for short-lived SIEM exports. goal: give SREs temporary access to high-fidelity logs for incident triage without broad, long-lived KMS or S3 perms. :thinking_face:
trent: +1. can you sketch constraints? retention, audit trail, RBAC boundaries?
maya: constraints: 1) exports live for max 24h, 2) envelope encrypted with customer KMS (service-key), but unwrap keys only via a short-lived grant, 3) audit events for grant issuance and export read must stream to Security SIEM channel, 4) masked PII by default except for approved incidents.
liam: quick q: how do we hand out the ephemeral creds? AWS STS assume-role with session policy limiting to the snapshot object? or issue pre-signed URLs?
maya: leaning assume-role + session policy so we get CloudTrail entries and can attach STS session tags (incident_id, approver). pre-signed URLs are easier but we lose fine-grained audit of who assumed.
nana: @maya small nit: we need to involve privacy for the masking rules. Also legal asked that PHI never leaves private net without a data-escrow process.
maya: noted — will loop privacy and legal. for PHI we'll require approval from privacy + 2FA approval from oncall.
trent: operationally, flow proposal: 1) SRE files incident ticket with tag export-needed, 2) security-bot opens an approval request to oncall + privacy, 3) once approved, a KMS Grant is created for 1 hour, 4) a signed URL + audit record produced and pushed to SIEM, 5) object TTL set to 24h then lifecycle delete.
liam: how do we avoid KMS grant sprawl? KMS limits grants per key can be high but we should revoke timely. maybe create a single ephemeral grant identity and rotate every 30m?
maya: we can use a single grant principal (export-service-role) and create/stamp ephemeral tokens rather than per-export grants. the grant allows decrypt for the service-role only; the export service enforces TTL and tags. revocation not needed per-export if we rotate the CMK key policy periodically, but that sucks for incident revocation.
nana: can we instead use a data-key approach: generate a data key (GenerateDataKey) under the CMK, encrypt payload with that data key, then wrap the data key with a short-lived encrypted envelope stored in SSM with an access policy? then revoking access to the envelope is simple.
trent: GenerateDataKey + envelope seems cleaner. sequence: 1) export-service calls KMS GenerateDataKey, receives plaintext DK and EncryptedDK, 2) encrypt logs with DK, 3) store EncryptedDK with metadata in a vault that supports time-bound grants (e.g., transient SSM/Secrets Manager entry with expiration), 4) grant access to vault entry to approvers.
liam: curious about audit visibility: we need CloudTrail for GenerateDataKey and Decrypt; also log which session-token or user triggered the Decrypt and link to incident_id. Tagging all KMS calls with session tags will help.
maya: yes — requirement: every KMS Decrypt/GenerateDataKey must include incident_id and approver in session tags. security-bot will assert tags in the approval flow.
nana: for SIEM ingestion: we should redact IPs and user identifiers in the exported logs by default. have a separate higher-fidelity snapshot endpoint for forensic ops that requires additional approvals and is stored in a different encrypted bucket with stricter retention.
trent: question on RBAC: which role should be allowed to request exports? SREs, SecOps, and SOC analysts? we need least privilege but not block triage.
liam: propose requesters = SRE_lead, SecOps_oncall, SOC_analyst-tier2. approvers = SecOps_manager + privacy on PHI. ops-oncall: thoughts?
ops-oncall: Ops supports that. just ask to include runbook link in the ticket so we can validate scope quickly.
maya: good call. I'll add runbook requirement. also adding an automatic pre-check that scan for PHI/PII and escalate to privacy if flagged.
trent: edge-case: what about exports triggered during active incident with an ongoing exploit? need immediate access. can we have an emergency bypass that logs a post-facto justification and sends to execs?
nana: we can allow emergency self-approve for oncall, but require 2hr postmortem justification + email to legal/privacy. log that as high-severity audit event.
liam: vuln triage note: exports must preserve integrity for forensic evidence — append-only storage for that bucket and no lifecycle delete until legal signoff. normal snapshot path remains TTL 24h.
maya: yep — bifurcate: forensic-bucket (WORM + legal hold) vs triage-bucket (24h TTL). CLI flags decide path, approval flow differs.
security-bot: AUTOMATION: created approval template `siem_jit_export_v1`. Fields: incident_id, approver, data_scope, PHI_flag, runbook_url. Trigger: /request-siem-export <incident_id>.
trent: sample session policy for the exporter (pseudocode):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"kms:GenerateDataKey","Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-...:key/AAA"},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::redwood-jit-exports/*"}
  ]
}
```
liam: add explicit Deny for kms:Decrypt unless session tag incident_id present. helps prevent accidental decrypt outside flow.
maya: action items: 1) draft design doc (I'll do) including sequence diagrams, 2) ops/runbook checklist for requesters (trent), 3) security infra PR for KMS envelope flow + vault gating (liam), 4) privacy/legal outreach (ana). owners assigned.
nana: I'll schedule a 30m sync for tomorrow to walk the privacy constraints.
trent: tagging follow-up: please include CloudTrail query examples so SOC can verify audit during triage.
liam: will add example CloudTrail queries to the doc.
ops-oncall: added runbook template to the ticket: https://go/repo/runbooks/siem-jit-export
maya: thanks — appreciate the fast feedback. we'll keep the export metadata small and machine-readable to make post-incident analytics easier. :thumbsup:
security-bot: NOTE: All approval actions will be recorded to channel #sec-approvals.
